messages:
mika: Heads-up: a customer reported unexpected invoice line items after a silent model fallback last week. We should standardize detection and surface an "explain bill" link in the console that ties routing decisions to billing rows.
jordan: Ugh. Are we sure this was a fallback and not a billing pipeline bug?
mika: Confirmed by request traces: intended_model=v2, served_model=v1, billed_rate_tag=v1. Tokens in metrics were attributed to v2 in some dashboards which made the reconciliation confusing.
lee: That mismatch is the root cause. Two separate systems used different fields: telemetry used intended_model while billing used served_model. We need a single source of truth and a reconciliation key.
sam.k: Proposal: attach a routing_id token to every request and persist it through traces -> metrics -> billing events. Expose routing_id in the console invoice view so CSMs/customers can trace the lifecycle.
jordan: Implementation-wise, adding routing_id to billing events sounds disruptive. Finance ok with new key?
billing-bot: FYI @finance IANA: adding routing_id is expected to be low risk, but we need a migration window to backfill historical data. Please ack.
infra-bot: Runtime note: we can emit a UUID in the request path, e.g., `X-Redwood-Routing-Id: <uuid4>` and ensure the edge, router, and compute layers carry it downstream. That should be trivial.
lee: Also need to align which model field is canonical in dashboards. I suggest 'served_model' should be canonical for billing and charge attribution. 'intended_model' remains useful for analytics.
sam.k: SDK change: when server returns a different served_model than requested, return a structured warning with code `MODEL_MISMATCH` and include routing_id. Example response snippet: ```json
{"error": null, "served_model":"redwood-v1.2", "intended_model":"redwood-v2", "routing_id":"abc-123", "warning_code":"MODEL_MISMATCH"}
``` This helps customers reconcile immediately.
mika: UX: Console invoice line should have a small 'why' link that opens a drawer with routing_id, served_model, intended_model, timestamp, routing_reason (capacity|timeout|error), and a 'contact CSM' button.
jordan: What about quotas? If v1 served the request, which quota bucket is decremented? Customers will be angry if v2 quota drops but billed at v1 or vice versa.
lee: Rule: quota decrement uses served_model's quota. Billing uses served_model's rate. Telemetry should report both intended and served, always.
billing-bot: We'll need to tag billable events with billed_rate_tag matching served_model. If router flips to v1, billed_rate_tag=v1. We'll coordinate with finance to make sure pricing tables map cleanly.
sam.k: Rollout plan: 1) telemetry + routing_id emission only (no behavior changes), 2) add structured SDK warnings + console invoice drilldown, 3) align billing pipeline to consume routing_id and billed_rate_tag, 4) add per-route policy toggle (strict/allow-fallback) and optional header `X-Redwood-Fallback: deny`.
mika: Can we also surface a daily 'fallback audit' for tenants affected >X times so CSMs can proactively reach out?
jordan: Good idea. Add an alert that triggers when fallbacks exceed 0.1% of route traffic for a day.
lee: One more: tests. We'll need integration tests that assert routing_id appears in traces, metrics, and billing events for simulated fallback scenarios.
infra-bot: I'll draft an infra RFC with implementation notes, pseudocode, and a feature-flag timeline. Pseudocode for edge emitter: ```
routing_id = uuid4()
set_header('X-Redwood-Routing-Id', routing_id)
set_header('X-Redwood-Intended-Model', requested_model)
// router decides served_model
set_header('X-Redwood-Served-Model', served_model)
emit_trace({routing_id, intended_model: requested_model, served_model})
```
sam.k: I'll update SDKs to include routing_id in the response object and add the MODEL_MISMATCH warning.
mika: I'll prototype the console invoice drawer copy and the 'fallback audit' email.
jordan: Assign owners and timeline in this thread please. We should aim to get phase 1 out in two weeks.
mika: Owners: infra-bot -> infra RFC (lee), SDK -> sam.k, console -> mika, billing coord -> jordan. Target: phase1 telemetry + routing_id in 14 days.
lee: noted. I'll start the RFC today and @infra-bot will create the feature flag branches.
sam.k: I'll open SDK PRs and small backwards-compatible tests.
mika: thanks everyone. We'll sync next Thursday for phase1 review. :calendar:
